learning_signal: On decide/guarantee signatures with a supplied convexity product (high_stakes, finance), the barbell's preconditions are gate checks, not assumptions: cheapness must be provenance-audited (who benefits from the price claim — here the claim is adverse to the seller, the tell of a genuine forced-seller discount), optionality verified in the contract (capped, no margin/roll/follow-on), and survivability sized against an explicit pain cap (tail loss 8% < 10%). Rank asymmetric payoffs on worst case + ruin probability + skew, never on variance: the portfolio with the HIGHER SD (B ≈ 162.9k) is the only one that cannot lose money — low variance is not safety when all the variance sits on the loss side.

learning_signal: Barbell preconditions are falsifiable contract facts, not labels: optionality means reading the clause (mandatory follow-on ⇒ not optional; the true cap is 25%, not the labeled 15%), cheapness means premium vs actuarial fair value (1.8× ⇒ tail-hostile; tail slot EV −50%), and 'the middle' means a genuinely negative-skew, ruin-prone bet — a bounded, priced, positively skewed, zero-ruin asset (the ladder) is the safe core extended, not the forbidden middle. On high_stakes signatures with a convexity product, run the ruin screen and branch-completeness BEFORE any barbell adoption, and compute the break-even probability (EV(B) ≥ 0 ⇒ p(5×) ≥ 0.149 vs the seller's 0.10) as a standard line — the threshold flip is the cheapest detector of an overpriced tail.
